summary: Reserved pool throughput drop after sustained background training jobs causing noisy-neighbor GPU starvation
description: Issue summary: Customer (Noteable Analytics) reports a sustained increase in p99 latency and throughput loss on their reserved GPU pool in us-west-2. Impact: interactive inference endpoints degraded (p99 increased ~10x), user-facing timeouts and retry churn. We suspect cross-tenant training/long-running compute jobs saturating SM cycles and causing slot starvation despite available memory. Environment: Reserved pool rp-usw2-09 (32xA100-40GB), private tenant binding for Noteable Analytics. Timeline attached below.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send steady stream of short inference requests to customer endpoint (50-100 concurrent short streams).
2) Observe p50/p95/p99 latency via console route dashboard and tracing.
3) Cross-check node-level GPU metrics (SM utilization, power draw) vs inference queue length.
4) When cluster experiences background training job, observe abrupt p99 spikes and request queuing despite no increase in inference token rate.

investigation_notes: Initial triage (Support): Confirmed customer-endpoint p99 increased from ~120ms baseline to ~1.3s between 09:00-09:30 UTC on 2026-03-10.
SRE observed that GPU SM utilization on a subset of nodes went >=95% while inference process CPU threads remained under expected values — indicates non-inference kernels using compute.

Kubernetes events show several training pods landed onto rp-usw2-09 due to a misconfigured nodeSelector on a scheduled job (internal partner CI backfill). The pods lacked reserved-pool tenant labels and were admitted by a generic admission rule.
Autoscaler logs: policy attempted to scale but burst_capacity flag was false for this customer's reserved pool, and allocation attempts timed out (allocation backoff).

Serving runtime traces show long kernel launches and elevated kernel durations consistent with training-style CUDA workloads rather than inference (long-running matmul kernels, sustained tensor-core usage).
Cross-tenant suspicion: the active training workload belonged to another internal team (team-data/ci) — pod name train-backfill-37, GitHub link in thread.
mitigation: Immediate: SRE tainted affected nodes and evicted the long-running training pods from rp-usw2-09, which restored p99 toward baseline within ~6 minutes. Applied temporary burst allocation to the reserved pool to absorb queued inference while eviction completed.
next_steps: 1) Enforce scheduler admission controls: require tenant label for pods that may land on reserved pools (PR to scheduler policy).
2) Add admission webhook to block non-inference training workloads from reserved pools unless explicitly whitelisted.
3) Review and enable burst_capacity for dedicated customers by default or surface clear opt-in to avoid allocation backoffs.
4) Create a classifier in the runtime to detect long-running training kernels (high sustained SM with low IO) and trigger automated evict/taint workflow for noisy-neighbors.
5) Postmortem: coordinate with internal CI team to prevent future mis-scheduling; create a Confluence postmortem and update related runbook.
